- Two-month history of progressive left shoulder pain with insidious onset

[GAPS]  
- Active and passive range of motion (especially forward flexion, abduction, external rotation) — critical to distinguish tendinopathy/impingement from adhesive capsulitis or glenohumeral pathology  
- Strength testing of individual rotator cuff muscles (e.g., supraspinatus, infraspinatus, subscapularis) — to assess for focal weakness suggesting tear or severe tendinopathy  
- Result of Neer’s impingement test  
- Result of Hawkins-Kennedy test  
- Result of resisted supraspinatus (empty can) test  
- Left shoulder ultrasound findings (tendon thickness, hypoechoicity, neovascularity, bursal fluid, AC joint morphology)  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Subacromial pain syndrome
